Pierre |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:153734-2 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |access-date=6 April 2025}} }} '''''Martiusella imperialis''''' is a tropical tree of the family [[Sapotaceae]] native to eastern Brazil. It is the sole species in genus '''''Martiusella'''''. It is currently classified as an [[endangered species]]. Its fruits were very much appreciated by the first emperor of Brazil, [[Pedro I of Brazil|Pedro I]] and his son [[Pedro II of Brazil|Pedro II]], who exported specimens of the tree as an offering to various botanical gardens around the world, including [[Sydney]] and [[Lisbon]].{{cite web |title=Árvores de Lisboa |date=21 August 2018 |url=https://revistabica.com/arvores-de-lisboa-3/ |publisher=revistabica.com |access-date=17 March 2021}} ==Distribution== It is [[endemic]] to the [[Atlantic Forest]] ecoregion of eastern [[Brazil]], native to the states of Bahia, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and São Paulo, including the vicinity of [[Rio de Janeiro]]. Most of its habitat has been erased by urbanisation and city spread.{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/gardening/stories/s938788.htm |title=Fact Sheet: Grow Your Own Threatened Species|last=Coleby-Williams|first=Jerry|date=5 September 2003|work=Gardening Australia website|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=11 January 2012}} It is a component of [[Serra do Mar coastal forests|lowland rainforest]] up to {{convert|800|m|ft|abbr=on}} elevation, where it grows to be a part of the [[Canopy (biology)|canopy]].{{cite web|url=http://botany.si.edu/projects/cpd/sa/sa15.htm|title=Mountain Ranges of Rio de Janeiro|last= Rejan R. Guedes-Bruni and Haroldo C. de Lima|work=Centres of Plant Diversity: The Americas|publisher= Department of Botany, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution.|access-date=12 January 2012|location=Washington, D.C.}} ==Description== ''Martiusella imperialis'' has large firm roundish cuneate-oblanceolate leaves, which measure {{convert|15|to|75|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|5|–|25|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} wide. They are smooth above and finely furred on the undersurface, and have a prominent midrib. The leaf margins are serrated, which is an unusual characteristic for the subfamily to which it belongs. ==Taxonomy== This species was first described in 1859 as ''Theophrastia imperialis'', before being given its current name by [[Joseph Dalton Hooker]] and [[George Bentham]]. It was also classified as ''Martusiella imperialis'' by French botanist [[Jean Baptiste Louis Pierre|J.B. Louis Pierre]] in 1891. It is known locally in Brazil as ''Marmelleiro do matto''.{{cite journal|last=Cronquist|first=Arthur|date=1946|title=Studies in the Sapotaceae-V. The South American Species of Chrysophyllum|journal=Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club|volume=73|issue=3|pages=286–311|doi=10.2307/2481670|jstor=2481670}} In 1991 it was placed in [[Section (botany)|section]] ''Aneuchrysophyllum'' of the genus ''Chrysophyllum'', along with ''[[Chrysophyllum bangweolense|C. bangweolense]]'' and ''[[Chrysophyllum venezuelanense|C. venezuelanense]]''. However a combined DNA and morphological study of the subfamily [[Chrysophylloideae]] found the two main genera, ''Chrysophyllum'' and ''[[Pouteria]]'', to be highly polyphyletic, and that ''C. imperiale'' is not closely related to other members of the genus but instead the genus ''[[Elaeoluma]]''. The study authors recommended resurrecting the binomial name ''Martusiella imperialis'' pending further resolution of relationships within the subfamily.{{Cite journal | last1 = Swenson | first1 = Ulf | last2 = Richardson | first2 = James E. | last3 = Bartish | first3 = Igor V. | doi = 10.1111/j.1096-0031.2008.00235.x | title = Multi-gene phylogeny of the pantropical subfamily Chrysophylloideae (Sapotaceae): Evidence of generic polyphyly and extensive morphological homoplasy | journal = Cladistics | volume = 24 | issue = 6 | pages = 1006–31 | year = 2008 | s2cid = 85192293 | doi-access = free }} ==Cultivation== An imposing specimen tree in the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Sydney]] was planted by [[Alfred, Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha|Prince Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh]] in 1868.{{cite web|url=http://www.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/education/Resources/BABQ/Tree_Truths|title=Tree Truths|work=Royal Botanic Gardens and Domain Trust|publisher=New South Wales Government|access-date=11 January 2012|location=Sydney, New South Wales|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120623110154/http://www.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/education/Resources/BABQ/Tree_Truths|archive-date=23 June 2012}} Seeds from this plant have been sent to Rio de Janeiro to facilitate recovery of the species there. Three specimens are growing in the Royal Botanic Gardens in Melbourne.{{cite web|url=http://www.rbg.vic.gov.au/dbpages/rbgcensus/index.php/census/species_detail/2799|title=''Chrysophyllum imperiale'' at the Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne|last=Royal Botanic Gardens, Melbourne|date=11 January 2012|work=Royal Botanic Gardens, Melbourne Website|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Board Victoria|access-date=12 January 2012|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055747/http://www.rbg.vic.gov.au/dbpages/rbgcensus/index.php/census/species_detail/2799|url-status=dead}} It can be grown as a container plant. ==References== {{Reflist|colwidth=26em}} ==External links== {{Commons category|position=left|Chrysophyllum imperiale}} {{Taxonbar|from= Q41799653|from2=Q41785315|from3=Q5114904}} [[Category:Chrysophylloideae]] [[Category:Sapotaceae genera]] [[Category:Monotypic Ericales genera]] [[Category:Endemic flora of Brazil]] [[Category:Flora of the Atlantic Forest]] [[Category:Flora of Northeast Brazil]] [[Category:Flora of Southeast Brazil]] [[Category:Endangered flora of South America]] [[Category:Taxa described in 1859]] [[Category:Taxa named by Karl Koch]]
